article_content: The saga surrounding radio DJ Casey Kasem's body has taken another unexpected turn with reports that his wife, Jean, is arranging to have it flown to Norway, contrary to his family's wishes. Kasem, known for hosting 'America's Top 40' and voicing 'Scooby-Doo's' Shaggy, died in June at 82 after battling dementia and Lewy body disease. His declining health sparked a heated family dispute over his care. Jean, married to Kasem for 34 years, has been embroiled in a bitter row with his three children from his first marriage. Kasem's daughter, Kerri, and the rest of the family are unaware of the current location of his body, which is believed to have been moved from a Washington funeral home to one in Montreal, Canada, according to reports. TMZ, citing sources close to the family, reports that Jean is planning to take the body abroad, possibly to Oslo, Norway.

article_content: By Ryan Gorman. PUBLISHED: 18:14 EST, 16 August 2013. UPDATED: 18:15 EST, 16 August 2013. Having not heard from Goldman Sachs after applying online, Michael Penn took matters into his own hands by handing out coffee and doughnuts on August 8 outside the bank's lower Manhattan headquarters. Facing the end of school with no job offers, Penn, 23, decided to stand out. He set up a table outside Goldman Sachs advertising a website with his resume and contact information. 'It is the pinnacle, it's everything we learn about in school, it is the top,' Penn told Fox Business. Though Penn didn't get an interview with Goldman Sachs, he had several interviews elsewhere and is grateful. Penn is graduating with a Master's in Global Management from Fordham University in two weeks and is looking for work in business development. The idea was to differentiate himself by doing something unique. 'It's just simple economics — supply and demand,' he told ABC News. His coffee cups had custom-made sleeves with his contact information and a short job-seeking pitch. Penn heard back from a potential employer soon after, who was intrigued by his ingenuity. 'My girlfriend saw you doing this, she took a picture,' the employer said. Penn attended the interview later that morning. Though he still has no job offers, Penn felt the drastic action was necessary to avoid living in his parents' basement. The setup cost Penn $150, funded by his mother for designing a website. His website lists his experience, degrees, and achievements, including being a US Chess Federation National Co-Champion at age nine. Despite the down economy and student loan debt, Penn remains hopeful. 'My life has changed for the better,' Penn said. Penn is among those who have used innovative means to find jobs during the Great Recession. In 2011, people put their faces on billboards in San Francisco's BART transit system. In 2009, Jamie Varon started TwitterShouldHireMe.com, which went viral, leading to a meeting with Twitter executives and eventually starting her own web design company, Shatterboxx.

article_content: By Ruth Styles. When Cay Garcia, a fifty-something from Cape Town, was offered a job with a Saudi princess, she accepted. Less than four months later, she was removed from the country after confronting her abusive employer. Now back in South Africa, she has written a book about her experiences. 'Life in Riyadh is harsh for women,' she says. 'Single women can't go for coffee alone.' The princess handed out harsh punishments, including beatings, to her staff. Cay wasn't physically harmed, but other maids were regularly abused. The iqama system prevents foreigners from leaving Saudi Arabia without their employer's permission. Cay's contract was terminated after several confrontations, and she was given an exit visa.

article_content: For thousands of years, the Thaua people, members of the Yuin nation in eastern Australia, had a unique whale hunting strategy with orcas in Twofold Bay, as described in a new study in the 'Journal of Heredity'. Thaua hunters worked with orcas to hunt whales, with some hunters singing to orcas to encourage them to herd whales inland. The orcas would eat the whales' lips and tongue, while the hunters took the rest. This practice, known as the 'Law of the Tongue,' lasted for generations until the 1930s, when the orcas vanished. DNA analysis of a 23-foot-long orca skeleton from almost 100 years ago, combined with Thaua knowledge, led scientists to believe the orca species is locally extinct.

Lovci z kmene Thaua spolupracovali s orkami při lovu velryb; někteří z nich dokonce zpívali, aby orky povzbudili k nahánění velryb směrem k pobřeží. Orky dostaly pysky a jazyk velryb, zatímco lovci si ponechali zbytek. Tato praxe, známá jako 'Zákon jazyka,' trvala po generace až do 30. let 20. století, kdy orky z oblasti zmizely. Analýza DNA kostry 23 stop dlouhé orky z doby před téměř 100 lety, zkombinovaná s vědomostmi lidu Thaua, vedla vědce k domněnce, že tento druh orky je v dané oblasti vyhynulý.

The discovery of this lens galaxy has now validated a key prediction made by 'Einstein's Theory of General Relativity'.

article_content: The world is getting hotter, and the sea is rising. A new report from the U.N. International Panel on Climate Change states that these changes are not natural. The report, compiled by over 800 authors and 50 editors from multiple countries, is the benchmark on climate change. It confirms that man-made climate change is 'almost certain.' Scientists are 95% confident that humans are responsible for at least half of the global temperature increase since the 1950s. The report notes that climate change affects extreme weather, such as record heat and heavy precipitation. The last 30 years are 'very likely' the warmest period in 800 years. Sea levels will rise due to warming oceans and melting ice. Climate change may persist for centuries even if emissions are halted.

article_content: Celebrity chef Heston Blumenthal has joined the Highclere Thoroughbred racing stable as a new owner. He expressed his excitement about joining Highclere Thoroughbred Racing, stating, 'I am thrilled to become an owner with Highclere Thoroughbred Racing. I have always enjoyed racing but never had the chance to own a horse until I met Harry Herbert at Ascot last year.' The horses he's invested in are all two-year-olds: Director, trained by William Haggas in Newmarket; Magnum, being prepared by Mikel Delzangles in France; Acolyte, trained by Roger Charlton; and Parish, trained by Roger Varian. Other notable owners in the Highclere syndicate include actors Hugh Bonneville and Elizabeth Hurley, athlete Denise Lewis, and former Manchester United manager Sir Alex Ferguson.

article_content: After a two-decade long manhunt, New Jersey authorities have apprehended James Wade Barclay, a convicted sex offender who was among the state's top 12 most-wanted fugitives. The arrest followed a multi-state investigation and a three-day stakeout. Barclay pleaded guilty in 1989 to sexually assaulting a 10-year-old multiple times over two years but failed to appear for his sentencing hearing in September 1991. He had since been on the run, creating a new identity as 'James Toryone' and working as a trucker across the United States. The investigation led police to a 'Stop N Ride' parking lot in rural Pennsylvania, where Barclay was arrested without incident on Saturday. He is being held in a Pennsylvania jail on '$5 million bail' and awaits extradition to New Jersey.

article_content: Russia and Ukraine are set to clash on the Eurovision Song Contest stage in Copenhagen, Denmark, on Saturday. The grand final, which follows the semi-finals, is expected to be a highly charged event due to the ongoing tensions between the two nations. The conflict in eastern Ukraine and Russia's annexation of Crimea have added a layer of complexity to the usual artistic competition. Eurovision, known for its extravagant performances and catchy pop songs, is meant to be a celebration of music that unites Europe. However, politics often plays a significant role in the voting process and performances. This was evident when Russia's representatives, 17-year-old twins Anastasia and Maria Tolmachevy, were booed during their semi-final performance. The booing was seen as a reaction to Russia's actions in Ukraine and its stance on LGBT issues. Ukraine's representative, 21-year-old Mariya Yaremchuk, expressed pride in representing her country and emphasized her connection to the Ukrainian people. The voting process, which involves both public votes and expert juries, is also subject to geopolitical influences, with former Soviet nations often voting for each other. The winner is determined by a points system, with the top scorer hosting the event the following year.

Evidence from Bull Creek in the Oklahoma Panhandle and an ice core from Greenland supports the comet impact theory.

article_content: The so-called 'Devil Comet' is approaching Earth and experiencing outbursts on its way around the sun. Known as 12P/Pons-Brooks, it hasn't appeared in Earth's skies for over 70 years. Its nucleus is estimated to be about 12.4 miles across, roughly twice Mount Everest's size. It will be visible next spring due to its brightness, not proximity. At its closest, it will be one-and-a-half astronomical units from Earth. The 'horns' are gas and dust tails from recent outbursts. Two outbursts occurred this year, in July and earlier this month. It'll reach peak brightness in mid-April 2024.

article_content: When you get a new tablet or smartphone, there are several steps you can take to make the most of it. First, turn on the screen-lock setting to add a layer of security. This will require a passcode, password, fingerprint, or face recognition every time you turn on your device. It's also a good idea to activate 'Find my iPhone' or 'Android Device Manager' to track your device if it's lost or stolen. Regular backups are essential; you can use 'iCloud', 'iTunes', or third-party services like 'Dropbox'. Getting a protective case is also recommended to prevent damage. To avoid unexpected charges, set a data limit on your device. Remove any preinstalled apps you don't need and download useful ones such as 'Twitter', 'Facebook', or 'Evernote'. For parents, setting up parental controls can help manage your kids' access to your device.

Je také rozumné aktivovat 'Najít můj iPhone' nebo 'Správce zařízení Android' pro sledování zařízení v případě ztráty nebo krádeže. Pravidelné zálohování dat je důležité; použijte 'iCloud', 'iTunes' nebo alternativní služby jako 'Dropbox'. Zvažte použití ochranného krytu, abyste předešli poškození. Jimmy served with the regiment for two years, carrying equipment and was taught to salute. The Cameronian's Museum awarded Jimmy the Dickin Medal, their highest honour for bravery.

article_content: The biological father of a Native American child was arrested on Monday after defying a court order to return the girl to her adoptive parents. This is the latest development in a four-year case that has spanned state lines and tested a federal law. Matt and Melanie Capobianco, a white couple from South Carolina, legally adopted Veronica at birth in September 2009. When Veronica's father, Dusten Brown, a member of the Cherokee Nation, learned of her adoption, he asserted his custody rights under the Indian Child Welfare Act, setting off a lengthy legal fight. A family court judge ruled in Brown's favor in late 2011, and he took his daughter back. The Capobiancos have fought to have Veronica returned. The case has gone from family court to the U.S. Supreme Court and back again. After South Carolina's Supreme Court ruled to allow the Capobiancos' adoption to be finalized, the U.S. Supreme Court refused to intervene, giving the Charleston couple the go-ahead to regain custody of Veronica. The girl's transition back to the Capobiancos was supposed to begin last week, but Brown never showed up with his daughter. A family court judge in South Carolina ordered the girl to be handed over, saying she was being 'unlawfully withheld from her lawful parents.' The Charleston County Sheriff's Office issued a warrant for Brown for interfering with custody. Brown was arrested in Oklahoma after turning himself in and posted a $10,000 bond. Melanie Capobianco said Veronica is being 'illegally held against the wishes of her parents and the courts,' and pleaded for her return. 'With every passing hour, we fear for her safety,' she said. Charleston County authorities are in touch with Oklahoma officials about extraditing Brown and locating 'Baby Veronica.' Brown said he is willing to go to jail for his daughter. 'I'm going to fight till I have no fight left,' Brown said.

Jedná se o nejnovější vývoj ve čtyřletém případu, který prověřil federální zákon. Pár z Jižní Karolíny, Matt a Melanie Capobianco, adoptoval Veroniku při narození v roce 2009. article_content: 'A Canadian amateur treasure hunter has unearthed a 16th-century coin on Vancouver Island, challenging the country's established history.' Bruce Campbell, a retired security systems installer, made the remarkable discovery using a hand-held metal detector. The coin, identified as an Edward VI shilling from between 1551 and 1553, has sparked debate about the early exploration of Canada's Pacific Coast. Historians have long believed that the Spanish were the first Europeans to set foot in British Columbia in 1774, followed by Captain James Cook four years later. However, the discovery has reignited speculation that Sir Francis Drake may have reached Canada's shores in 1579, two centuries before the Spanish. Samuel Bawlf, an advocate for the 'Drake theory,' suggests the coin supports the idea that Drake traveled further north than previously thought. Not everyone is convinced; Royal British Columbia Museum curator Grant Keddie remains skeptical due to a lack of concrete evidence.

Bruce Campbell, důchodce a bývalý montér bezpečnostních systémů, učinil tento pozoruhodný objev pomocí ručního detektoru kovů. Mince, určená jako šilink Eduarda VI. z let 1551 až 1553, vyvolala debatu o prvotním průzkumu kanadského pacifického pobřeží. Historici dlouho věřili, že Španělé byli první Evropané, kteří vkročili do Britské Kolumbie v roce 1774, následováni kapitánem Jamesem Cookem o čtyři roky později. Nicméně objev znovu podnítil spekulace, že Sir Francis Drake mohl dosáhnout kanadských břehů už v roce 1579, dvě století před Španěly. Samuel Bawlf, zastánce teorie o Drakeově cestě, tvrdí, že mince podporuje myšlenku, že Drake putoval dále na sever, než se dříve předpokládalo. Ne každý je však přesvědčen; kurátor Royal British Columbia Museum, Grant Keddie, zůstává skeptický kvůli nedostatku konkrétních důkazů.

article_content: The wonderful weather brings open windows, outdoor eating, and unfortunately, lots of flies, wasps, and mosquitoes. So, what can you do to beat the little biters? We tested six different solutions. Cruel: This high-tech swatter doesn't always kill flies but can injure them. The 'Executioner Bug Zapper Racket', £10.99 on amazon.co.uk, is a battery-operated racket that emits a static charge to 'zap' flies, mosquitoes, and wasps. Pros: It's sturdier and more powerful than some alternatives. Cons: It's cruel and doesn't always kill flies. VERDICT: 1/5 Cute but ineffective: 'Lovebug Electronic Mosquito Deterrent', £9.95 on johnlewis.com. Designed to protect babies from mosquitoes, this device emits a low-level tone imitating a dragonfly's wing beat. Pros: No insecticides or chemicals are involved. Cons: It failed to deter mosquitoes in our test. VERDICT: 0/5 The 'Waspinator': Not pretty but could keep wasps away. Waspinator, £9.50 for a set of two on qvc.com. This grey bag is designed to deter wasps by mimicking a real nest. Pros: It's a cheap and natural way to deter wasps. Cons: May not work if there's an established nest nearby. VERDICT: 3/5 Useless: Plastic bag filled with water and copper coins. Pros: It's cheap and easy to make. Cons: Didn't work in our test. VERDICT: 0/5 Small but powerful: The 'Prevent Scentrel' candle, £5.99 from Robert Dyas stores. This candle, infused with pyrethrin, repels mosquitoes, flies, midges, and wasps. Pros: Effective and almost odourless. Cons: Requires caution when burning. VERDICT: 4/5 Useful but unattractive: 'Adjustable Insect Repellent Block', £3.79 on lakeland.co.uk. Contains permethrin, a powerful insecticide. Pros: Compact and has a pleasant fragrance. Cons: Unattractive appearance and confusing claims. VERDICT: 2/5

article_content: By Helen Pow PUBLISHED: 09:31 EST, 29 April 2013 | UPDATED: 09:54 EST, 29 April 2013 Five boyhood buddies injured while watching another friend run in the Boston Marathon are now helping each other recover from the life-changing blasts. After the first bomb went off near the finish line of the April 15 race, brothers Paul and J.P. Norden huddled with long-time pals Jarrod Clowery, Marc Fucarile, and James 'Bim' Costello, not realizing they were inches away from the second device. When it blew, both brothers and Fucarile lost a leg, while Clowery suffered burns and shrapnel wounds, and Costello was hospitalized with serious injuries. Two weeks and numerous surgeries later, the friends' health is improving, but the tight bond, cemented through years of fishing trips and poker games, is what is helping them pull through. 'What's up, kid?' Clowery, 35, asked Paul Norden, 31, who is in Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center recovering from having his right leg amputated. Clowery is being treated for burns at Brigham and Women's Hospital, but another friend pushed him, still dressed in his hospital gown, the two blocks so he could visit his pal. 'Yeah, dude, I escaped,' he said. 'I had to see you. I had to come.' Paul's older brother, J.P., 33, is just two doors down from Clowery at Brigham and Women's recovering from his own amputation, while Fucarile is at Massachusetts General Hospital. Mike Jefferson, the school buddy they came to cheer on at the marathon, was the only one spared. Feeling guilty he dragged his pals along that fateful day, he now keeps watch over them, sleeping outside Paul Norden's hospital room in case he needs anything. 'He blames himself,' Norden told The Boston Globe. 'But I told him: It's not your fault. That bridge has passed. We have to get to a new place.' The men, who met at elementary school or youth clubs in the small Massachusetts town of Stoneham, grew up at each other's houses, though the Norden brothers' mom, Liz, who they all called 'Ma,' tended to play host. They all found jobs in the construction industry, but the past winter had been a brutal one with work slowing and paychecks stretching thin. Now they face months of rehabilitation, and the Norden brothers and Fucarile must learn to walk again using prosthetic legs. Paul Norden is set to be transferred to a rehabilitation hospital this week, but his main concern is that his brother, who is not yet ready to leave Brigham, ends up at the same one. 'I have to go to rehab with my brother,' he told The Globe. Emotional, Paul Norden recalled the first phone call the brothers, who still haven't seen each other, shared after the tragedy, when they each learned the other had lost a leg. It ended: 'I love you. We'll get through this no matter what.' The Stoneham community and others are fundraising to help the friends pay for their treatment.

Nordenovi se přikrčili k dlouholetým kamarádům Jarrodu Clowerymu, Marcovi Fucarilemu a Jamesovi 'Bim' Costellovi, aniž si uvědomili, že jsou pár centimetrů od druhého zařízení. article_content: Zimbabweans are bracing themselves for the verdict Friday in the treason trial of opposition leader Morgan Tsvangirai, who is widely believed to be innocent. If found guilty Mr. Tsvangirai could face the 'so-called' death sentence. Morgan Tsvangirai is accused of hiring Canadian businessman Ari Ben Menashe to plot the 'alleged' assassination of President Robert Mugabe before presidential elections in March 2002. The year-long trial concluded last February and Mr. Tsvangirai has been waiting since then for the verdict. Political commentator and human rights activist Brian Kagoro said the charges, coming as they did when the Movement for Democratic Change, MDC, was only 30-months-old, has almost 'totally destroyed' the party. He said the two top MDC leaders, who had to surrender their passports because of the trial, were unable to travel in Africa to explain the young party's policies. Mr. Kagoro, co-chairman of the Zimbabwe Crises Coalition, said the trial had also crippled the Movement for Democratic Change financially and forced it to scale down its political protests to avoid aggravating the treason charges. The state relied on two pieces of evidence, Mr. Ben Menashe's testimony, and a tape he secretly recorded when he met Mr. Tsvangirai in Canada in late 2001. The state said the tape recording proved that Mr. Tsvangirai tried to hire Mr. Menashe for the assassination plot. Mr. Tsvangirai denies the charge and says the conversation recorded in Canada was a discussion about possible political scenarios ahead of the presidential poll, including the possibility of Mr. Mugabe's sudden death and its constitutional implications. Mr. Tsvangirai's two colleagues, one of them MDC Secretary-General Welshman Ncube, were earlier acquitted for lack of evidence. Mr. Tsvangirai was defended by famed South African advocate George Bizos, who defended former South African President Nelson Mandela on similar charges 40 years ago. Mr. Bizos argued that Mr. Ben Menashe had set out to entrap his client. He also described Mr. Ben Menashe as an 'undisputed' liar, and international crook. Mr. Ben Menashe accused Mr. Bizos of being a well-known racist. The court established that Mr. Ben Menashe was paid '$615,000' by the Zimbabwe government for securing the tape recording and for publicity work for Mr. Mugabe.

Pokud bude shledán vinným, mohl by čelit 'takzvanému' trestu smrti. Morgan Tsvangirai je obviněn z najmutí kanadského podnikatele Ariho Bena Menasheho, aby spikloval 'údajnou' vraždu prezidenta Roberta Mugabeho před prezidentskými volbami v březnu 2002. Roky trvající proces skončil loni v únoru a pan Tsvangirai od té doby čeká na verdikt. article_content: BEIRUT - Syria's parliament has imposed strict residency rules for presidential candidates, state media reported on Friday, a decision that would effectively eliminate many of President Bashar al-Assad's opponents who reside in exile as the major Arab state's uprising enters its fourth year. Assad has not yet confirmed whether he will run for a third term, defying rebels fighting to overthrow him and Western leaders who have called for his resignation to help end Syria's civil war and pave the way for a democratic transition. The Syrian state news agency SANA stated that 'Section 30 of the draft law stipulates that candidates for the office of president of the republic must ... have maintained continuous, permanent residence in the Syrian Arab Republic for a period of no less than 10 years at the time of seeking nomination.' Many opposition members have lived outside Syria since before the revolt began in March 2011, and more left during the subsequent security crackdown. The Western-backed Syrian National Coalition maintains a provisional government for rebel-held areas based in Istanbul.

article_content: A man widely reported to be a 'prime' suspect in last week's deadly Brussels terrorist attacks has been released due to 'insufficient' evidence. Belgium's federal prosecutor stated on Monday that authorities had no grounds to detain the man, identified as Faycal C. Before his release, Faycal C. faced preliminary charges of 'participating in a terrorist organization, terrorist murder, and attempted terrorist murder.' Media reports indicated that his name was Faycal Cheffou and that he was believed to be the third individual captured on airport security camera footage alongside the two men who detonated explosives. The Belgian federal police released a photo showing a screengrab of airport CCTV footage of the suspects involved in the attacks at Brussels Airport on March 22, 2016. It remains unclear whether investigators believe he is the man seen in the grainy CCTV photo taken moments before the blast. Earlier on Monday, police released additional airport surveillance footage and solicited public assistance in identifying the man, who was wearing a hat and a white jacket. The three men in the footage were pushing suitcases believed to contain explosives through the airport departure hall. Two of the men were killed in the blasts, while the third man, whose bomb failed to detonate, has been the subject of an intense manhunt. The attacks occurred simultaneously with an attack on the Brussels metro, resulting in 35 fatalities and approximately 300 injuries. A girl lit candles as people paid tribute to the victims of the bomb attacks at the Place de la Bourse in Brussels, Belgium, on March 26, 2016. Authorities conducted repeated raids in and around the capital to disrupt what appears to be a 'well-organized' and 'expansive' terrorist network. On Monday, Brussels prosecutors charged three individuals with involvement in a terrorist group. The charged individuals were identified as Yassine A., Mohamed B., and Aboubaker O. No additional details were released, and the prosecutors did not directly indicate whether the suspects were involved in the Brussels attack. Heather Murdock contributed to this report from Brussels.
